en.p: In coordinate space there are two spheres

Let $\alpha$ be the plane that passes through the point $\mathrm{A}(\sqrt{5},\,0,\,0)$, is perpendicular to the $zx$-plane, and is tangent to sphere $S_1$ at a point with positive $z$-coordinate. Let $C$ be the circle formed where sphere $S_2$ meets plane $\alpha$, let B be the point on circle $C$ with the least $z$-coordinate, and let $\beta$ be the plane tangent to $S_2$ at point B.
When the area of the orthogonal projection of circle $C$ onto plane $\beta$ is $\dfrac{q}{p}\pi$, find the value of $p+q$. (Here $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
